story_type: rocket engine test ends short of its scheduled full duration
hook: This Moon rocket engine was scheduled for a full run.
narration: This Moon rocket engine was scheduled to fire for its full duration. It fell short.
December fourteenth, 2022, on a test stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi.
It was an RS-25, the engine built for future flights of the Space Launch System.
NASA modified sixteen engines left over from the shuttle program to fly the first four Artemis missions.
This firing opened the testing for the engines that fly from Artemis Five on.
It burns liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, so its exhaust is mostly water vapor. That is the white cloud.
NASA called it a confidence test, a check that everything was ready for certification firings early the next year.
[short pause] Then, before the scheduled full duration, the engine shut down.
outcome: The RS-25 fired for two hundred nine and a half seconds of its scheduled full duration test.
title: Moon rocket engine test cut short
description:
On Dec. 14, 2022, NASA fired an RS-25 rocket engine at Stennis Space Center in Mississippi, completing 209.5 seconds of a scheduled full-duration hot fire in the first test of a new engine campaign for future Space Launch System flights.

facts.claim: Dec. 14 test at Stennis completed 209.5 seconds of a scheduled full-duration hot fire
facts.source_quote: NASA conducted the first test of the new RS-25 restart engine campaign for future flights of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket Dec. 14, completing 209.5 seconds of a scheduled full-duration hot fire at Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi.

facts.claim: Confidence test before certification tests early next year
facts.source_quote: The single-engine hot fire, known as a confidence test, was designed to confirm all is ready to proceed with a series of certification tests early next year on a full RS-25 certification engine.

facts.claim: Sixteen leftover shuttle engines modified for Artemis I through IV
facts.source_quote: NASA and the company modified 16 of the engines remaining after the Space Shuttle Program for use on Artemis mission I through IV.

facts.claim: This testing is for engines beginning with Artemis V
facts.source_quote: The upcoming series of testing is for the RS-25 engines that will be used beginning with Artemis V.
